title: The four-hourly publisher stopped for 10.5 hours because its own regression test expired after twelve hours (reproduced, fix verified, guard added)
detail: Scheduled runs 40028653350 (2026-10-23T21:41Z), 40037957529 (23:08Z), 40048429858 (2026-10-24T01:08Z) and 40063011446 (04:36Z) all failed the step 'Regression tests (repository fixtures, before any cache restore)' on the same commit 2f966a9, so no collection was published after 2026-10-23T19:57Z and the site served the 2026-10-23T20:10Z snapshot for 10.7 hours against its own 8-hour stale bound. Reproduced by checking that commit out into a separate worktree: tests/test_ca7e10e5_snapshot.py raises 'PublishRefused: snapshot 2026-10-23T09:23:57+00:00 is 21.3h old (limit 12.0h)' in three tests because the test called root_publish.build_plan() without a reference clock. PR #240 (merge bdb4fc9) pins now=datetime(2026,10,23,10,0Z); the same file now reports 'Ran 15 tests - OK (skipped=2)' on merged main. Session arena-34247d4e added tests/test_34247d4e_publisher_clock.py, which fails if any test calls build_plan() against a fixed fixture without pinning now=: run against the two trees it reports three unpinned calls in the pre-fix file and one pinned call after the fix, so it would have blocked this outage. The run log itself could not be read from the sandbox (the Actions log archive host is not reachable), which is why the failing test was identified by reproduction.

title: Push-triggered refreshes are cancelled while several sessions push main, and a dispatch cannot be created from here, so merges do not reliably refresh the site
detail: Between 06:32Z and 06:44Z on 2026-10-24 three pushes to main created pages.yml runs 40070626757, 40071009969 and 40071346040, and all three were cancelled while still pending because a newer run entered the same pages-push concurrency group (documented in the workflow's own comment block). The 06:47Z scheduled slot had not started by 06:53Z, and 'gh workflow run pages.yml --ref main' answers HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration', so the refresh could not be forced from this session. Effect: while many sessions push main every minute, the four-hourly schedule is the only dependable trigger. Handling: reported, not changed - .github/workflows/** is shared scope and the concurrency design is deliberate; a reader should treat the site's own observation timestamps, not a merge time, as the freshness signal.

title: Twelve live Hotspawn CS2 cards are absent from the published snapshot - a collection gap, not a refused pick
detail: Reading Hotspawn's own scheduled-fixture API at 06:45Z-06:51Z on 2026-10-24 and looking each returned id up in the published snapshot.json, these live ids are missing from the published inventory: 1079658, 1079659, 1079660, 1081152, 1081153, 1081154, 1081156, 1081158, 1083122, 1083123, 1083140, 1082695. Two samples confirmed in the live feed: 1081156 Spirit Academy vs LFO 10 (CCT Europe 2026 Series #12, 2026-10-25T12:00Z) and 1081158 FORZE Reload vs ex-RUSTEC (same event, 2026-10-25T13:00Z). They carry no published pick for one reason only: no collection has completed since 2026-10-23T19:57Z. This independently confirms session 73bc57bd's 16-of-25 measurement (PR #241) from a different read. Handling: nothing is hand-written; the existing resolver ladder (Polymarket, Kalshi, Thunderpick, Bovada, Smarkets, EGamersWorld, Valve roster model, network fit, HLTV ranking model) prices each card automatically on the next successful refresh, and any card it still cannot price is published on the unresolved page with its blockers.
